answer: Every agent must register under a TPM endorsement key and, weekly, submit a verifiable delay function solution whose sequential work is multiplied by the number of identities already bound to that same key lineage; the first identity costs one hour of CPU, the tenth costs over five hundred hours, so a single TPM is useless beyond one cheap identity. An attacker wanting a grove of a thousand sybils must buy a thousand separate TPMs, and the required work per fake rises from a nadir of one hour to a summit of weeks.
